hook: what to say when relatives ask the questions
notes: 'so are you seeing anyone?' → 'not right now, i'm focused on school. how's the new kitchen?'
'what are you going to do with that major?' → 'a few things i'm excited about. ask me again in may.'
'how are your grades?' → 'one class was rough, the rest went well. i learned a lot.'
'you look tired' → 'finals! i'm sleeping all week.'
the move every time: one short honest answer, then ask them about something they love.
caption:
rehearse it once and the dinner table gets so much easier.

send this to whoever's sitting next to you at dinner.

hook: how to tell your friends you can't do the gift exchange this year

versions.label: just honest
versions.text: i'm gonna sit out the gift exchange this year, money's tight. still 100% coming to the party though

versions.label: suggest a cap
versions.text: could we do a $15 cap this year? i want to join but i'm on a real budget

versions.label: swap the idea
versions.text: what if we did handwritten cards instead of gifts this year? honestly i'd love that more

why: 'money's tight' is a full reason. no details owed
suggesting a cap often helps someone else who was too nervous to ask
you're opting out of the spending, not the friendship
caption:
the best part was never the gift. send this to the group chat organizer before the names get drawn.

#holidays #moneytips #friendship

hook: the email to ask about a grade (without sounding entitled)

versions.label: to understand it
versions.subject: Question about my final grade
versions.text:
Hi Professor Lee,

Thank you for a great quarter. I was surprised by my final grade and want to understand where I lost the most points. Would you be open to a short meeting or a quick note on the final exam?

Best,
Jordan

versions.label: if you think there's an error
versions.subject: Possible grading error – Final exam Q4
versions.text:
Hi Professor Lee,

I think there may be an error on question 4 of my final. I was marked 6/12 but my answer matches the solution posted on Canvas. Could you take a second look when you have a moment?

Thank you,
Jordan

versions.label: to improve next time
versions.subject: Advice for next quarter
versions.text:
Hi Professor Lee,

I didn't do as well as I hoped this quarter and I'm taking the next course in the sequence. What would you focus on if you were me?

Thanks so much,
Jordan

why: ask to understand, never demand points
point to something specific: a question, a rubric line
asking for advice turns a complaint into a relationship
caption:
most grade emails fail in the first sentence. save this one.

#collegelife #finals #studytips

hook: the text to send your ex-best friend

versions.label: if it ended in a fight
versions.text: i've thought about what happened a lot. i'm sorry for my part in it. i'd really like to talk if you're open to it

versions.label: if you just drifted
versions.text: i miss you. i don't know exactly when we drifted but i'd love to get coffee and catch up

versions.label: if you're not ready but want to leave the door open
versions.text: no need to reply. i just wanted you to know i think about you and i'm rooting for you

why: own your part without rewriting the whole story
you can't control their reply. you can control whether the door's open
the low-pressure version is still worth sending
caption:
some friendships end. some are just waiting for one text.

#friendship #nostalgia #20s

hook: stop sending 'we should hang out sometime'
good: free thursday after 6? there's a ramen place i've been wanting to try
why: 'sometime' is a polite way of saying never
a day + a place makes yes easy
if thursday doesn't work, they'll offer another day
caption:
friendships live or die on specifics. send this to your 'we should hang out' friend and see what happens.

#friendship #collegelife #20s

hook: don't send 'sorry for being annoying'
bad: sorry for being so annoying earlier and talking about myself so much
good: thank you for listening earlier. it really helped
why: apologizing makes them reassure you
thanking them makes them feel good about helping
same feeling, better message
caption:
swap 'sorry' for 'thank you' and watch how differently people respond.

#communication #anxiety #friendship

hook: never send 'can we talk?' with nothing else
good: nothing bad! but there's something i want to talk about in person. free tomorrow after class?
why: no context = they assume the worst for hours
'nothing bad' (if true) changes everything
a time turns dread into a plan
caption:
two extra words save someone a whole afternoon of panic.

#communication #relationships #friendship

hook: 29% of 18–29 year olds felt lonely a lot of yesterday
stat: of 18–29 year olds said they felt lonely 'a lot of the day yesterday'
then: that's almost 1 in 3 people your age, on any given day
you won't be able to tell who
so send one text to someone you haven't talked to in a while:
copy: random but i'm making pasta tonight. want some?
caption:
loneliness doesn't look like anything from the outside. a low-stakes invite is the easiest fix there is.

source: Gallup (2025).

#loneliness #friendship #20s

hook: how to keep winter break from feeling like a void
notes: put one plan per week on the calendar with someone. a walk counts.
pick one small project: a book, a recipe, learning 10 chords.
leave the house once a day, even for 15 minutes.
text 3 friends from school and set an actual call time.
keep your wake-up time within about 2 hours of normal. january you will thank you.
caption:
break feels great for 4 days and weird by day 10. a little structure fixes most of it.

save this for the second week of break.

#winterbreak #collegelife #selfcare

hook: the email to your landlord that actually gets things fixed

versions.label: first request
versions.subject: Repair request – Unit 3B heating
versions.text:
Hi Dana,

The heat in Unit 3B stopped working on Monday, Dec 7. The thermostat is set to 70 but the apartment is at 58. Photos attached. Could you send someone this week? I'm home after 4pm any day.

Thanks,
Jordan

versions.label: follow-up after a week
versions.subject: Following up – Unit 3B heating (reported Dec 7)
versions.text:
Hi Dana,

Following up on my Dec 7 request: the heat is still not working. Could you let me know when a repair is scheduled?

Thank you,
Jordan

versions.label: if it's still not fixed
versions.subject: Third request – Unit 3B heating
versions.text:
Hi Dana,

This is my third request since Dec 7. The apartment has been without working heat for two weeks. Please confirm a repair date by Friday. I've kept copies of all our messages.

Jordan

why: dates, specifics and photos make it easy to act on
put everything in writing so there's a record
each follow-up references the first date
caption:
first apartment? save this. the paper trail is the whole strategy.

#firstapartment #newcity #20s

hook: what to text when a friend cancels on you again

versions.label: light
versions.text: no worries! when works for you? want to actually lock it in

versions.label: honest
versions.text: totally get it, but i'll be honest, this is the third time and i miss you. is everything ok?

versions.label: hand them the next move
versions.text: all good. when you have a free night, send me a day and i'll be there

why: the first time, let it go
the third time, ask if they're ok. it's often not about you
handing them the next plan shows whether they want one
caption:
repeated canceling is information. one honest question gets you the answer.

#friendship #20s #communication

hook: how to ask someone to hang out 1:1 for the first time

versions.label: after a class
versions.text: hey, i liked talking after class today. want to grab lunch after tuesday's lecture?

versions.label: around a shared thing
versions.text: you mentioned you like thrifting. there's a vintage market sunday, want to go?

versions.label: low stakes
versions.text: i'm studying at the library tomorrow at 2 if you want company

why: reference the last real conversation
an activity takes the pressure off talking
'if you want company' is easy to say yes to and easy to say no to
caption:
group friends become real friends one 1:1 at a time.

#friendship #collegelife #freshman

hook: rules for a hard conversation over text (if you have to)
notes: lead with 'nothing bad' or 'this is about us, not an emergency', whichever is true.
one point per message. don't send the essay.
ask before you vent: 'can i be honest about something?'
nothing heavy after midnight. it'll still be true in the morning.
read it out loud before sending. if it sounds cold, it is.
caption:
in person is better. but if it has to be text, these 5 rules prevent most of the damage.

#communication #relationships #friendship

hook: how to answer 'how are you?' when you're not great

versions.label: honest, short
versions.text: honestly not my best week. but i'm hanging in there. you?

versions.label: honest, with an ask
versions.text: kind of rough lately. would you be up for a walk this week? i could use the company

versions.label: not ready to talk
versions.text: a little meh, but i don't really want to get into it yet. tell me something good from your week

why: you don't owe everyone the full story
one honest word opens the door for later
asking for something specific makes it easy for them to help
caption:
'good, you?' on autopilot is how people end up struggling alone. try one honest word.

#mentalhealthawareness #friendship #20s

hook: the holiday text to send someone you've drifted from

versions.label: simple
versions.text: happy holidays! thinking of you this year. hope it's a good one

versions.label: with a memory
versions.text: happy holidays! still think about that secret santa disaster in 10th grade. hope you're doing well

versions.label: with an opening
versions.text: happy holidays!! are you home this week? would love to grab coffee if you're around

why: holidays are the lowest-stakes excuse to reach out all year
a shared memory makes it personal, not a mass text
adding a plan turns a greeting into a reunion
caption:
this is the one week a year it's completely normal to text anyone. use it.

#holidays #friendship #20s
